name: FOREIGN EXCHANGE STUDENTS
notes: All etymologies and dates verified (yen 1871, rand 1961, forint/florin 1946, quetzal 1925 incl. Maya feather-money); quetzal slightly soft for $2000.

name: PAST TENDER
notes: Pre-euro facts all check out; deutsche-mark clue's hook is the mildest of the five but clean and fair.

name: THE DISMAL SCIENCE FAIR
notes: Macleod 1965 stagflation coinage and Gresham attribution correct; strong stair-step ladder.

name: WORD ON THE STREET
notes: Ponzi/arbitrage/tontine all accurate; tontine is a satisfying $2000 with the mystery-plot hook.

name: THE PHILANTHROPIST'S STONE
notes: Hopkins bequest, Walker's hedged 'cited as', and Peabody's London housing + Harvard/Yale museums all verified.

name: FORTUNE 500 B.C.
notes: Facts solid (Fugger/Charles V, Mansa Musa's Cairo gold); 'B.C.' pun stretched by Medici/Mansa Musa/Fugger being A.D. — fit docked one.

name: THIS TOO SHALL POP
notes: Fixed $1200: 'paid thousands for Princess the Bear' overstated craze-era prices (~$200s; 'thousands' is later eBay myth) — rewrote as Diana-tribute holy-grail clue, no price claim.

name: CHAPTER 11 & VERSE
notes: All five collapses accurate; Woolworth never actually filed Chapter 11 (clue's claims are true) — name fit docked one.

name: WHERE CREDIT IS DUE
notes: banca rotta, Juno Moneta, Exchequer cloth, pecus, bursa — every etymology is textbook-correct.

name: COUNTER CULTURE
notes: Mottoes and founders verified; Harrods $400 leans on the Latin motto but 'Knightsbridge emporium' keeps it gettable.

name: BUY THE BOOK
notes: L.L. Bean 90/100 lore and Tiffany 1845 Blue Book verified by search; Bean at $1200 arguably easier than Ward at $800 — minor mid-ladder wobble.

name: DOUBLOON OR NOTHING
notes: Atocha/Amber Room details correct; Klondike clue's 'this Canadian region' could also draw 'the Yukon' — mild specificity ding.
